consensus_summary: Primary identification of 'heart of the earth' (Matt 12:40) as Jesus' burial in the tomb/grave or sojourn in the realm of the dead (Sheol/Hades) for three days and nights, as the antitype of Jonah in the fish; Jerusalem/land readings appear only as minority or rare alternatives.
book_summary: Jerusalem as the navel and heart of the land.
consensus_core_identification: Christ's tomb/grave or Hades/Sheol (the place of death and burial)
boundary_disagreement: Consensus centers the three days on the burial interval (tomb or underworld); the book reassigns the entire phrase to Jerusalem itself, shifting the spatial and chronological boundaries to the city/land and events such as arrest or custody.
material_contradiction: Book equates the phrase with Jerusalem; consensus equates it with the tomb or Hades. These cannot be the same referent in the same sense.
rationale: Consensus responses converge on tomb/Hades as the settled core while listing the Jerusalem reading only as a minority alternative. The book discards that core and installs the minority identification as its sole entry, producing a replaced rather than refined or overlapping referent. The relation is therefore divergent, not refined or novel.
strongest_objection: The explicit Jonah parallel in Matt 12:40 most naturally identifies the 'heart of the earth' with the place of confinement after death (tomb/Hades), not with the city of Jerusalem.
